root_cause_analysis.observed_reason: A pending review_decision_intent durably fences every task mutation and dispatch until the exact same actor replays the exact same command/message/nonce (AI_COLLABORATION_GUIDE.md section 3). scripts/ai_status.py already supports that idempotent replay, but .orchestrator/supervisor.py's task_execution_dispatch_candidate() and evaluate_task_delivery_admission() both treat any pending review_decision_intent as an unconditional Human/Ops hold. If the reviewer worker that reserved the intent loses its lease (crash, restart, lease reap) before replaying it, no worker -- including the original actor -- is ever dispatched again to retry it. The task becomes a permanent deadlock recoverable only by a human running the exact ai-status.sh command by hand.
findings: .orchestrator/supervisor.py task_execution_dispatch_candidate() returned None unconditionally whenever review_decision_intent was pending, with no path back to dispatch even for the original reserving actor.

.orchestrator/supervisor.py evaluate_task_delivery_admission() set TaskIntent.human_ops_hold=True unconditionally on a pending review_decision_intent, which reserve_dispatch_plan() revalidates on every event before launch, so no supervisor-built recovery event could ever pass admission either.

No supervisor-owned mechanism observed the reserving worker's lease independently of the intent itself, so nothing detected 'the worker that reserved this decision is gone' and nothing authorized a narrow, exact-actor replay dispatch.

remediation.recovery_receipt: .orchestrator/rewrite/review_intent_recovery.py adds a typed, generation-bound recovery receipt (review_decision_intent_recovery) that binds the pending intent's exact nonce/actor/command/message plus the task's current generation and CAS digest. Its own task-row field, and the intent's, are excluded from review_decision_task_digest (mirrored in scripts/ai_status.py) so minting or clearing the receipt can never perturb the frozen CAS binding the intent reserved.
remediation.lease_detection: supervisor.review_decision_intent_lease_is_lost() treats a pending intent's reservation as lost only once it has outlived one full worker-lease window AND no live worker record still holds an unexpired lease on the task -- both conditions guard against racing a reservation that is still legitimately in flight.
remediation.receipt_minting: supervisor.reconcile_review_decision_intent_lease_recovery() runs on every poll cycle (wired alongside reconcile_pending_worker_recoveries in both poll_workers and the boot reconciliation path) and durably CAS-writes the recovery receipt via persist_review_decision_intent_recovery_receipt() without touching owner, reviewer, generation, or any other field the intent's digest depends on.
remediation.narrow_replay_admission: supervisor.review_decision_intent_replay_eligible() is the single eligibility predicate, reused by task_execution_dispatch_candidate() (so the exact original actor falls through to ordinary REVIEW_READY/OWNED_* reason computation instead of being unconditionally fenced) and evaluate_task_delivery_admission() (so human_ops_hold is False only for that exact actor). Every other agent, and any stale or generation-mismatched receipt, still hits the unconditional fence -- this is what prevents impersonation and keeps generic workers fenced.
remediation.replay_instructions: build_dispatch_event() injects the exact replay command (AI_NAME=<actor> ai-status.sh <command> <task_id> "<message>") into that one dispatch event's task payload 'next' field when the eligibility check passes, without ever mutating the canonical (frozen) task row's own 'next' field.
remediation.cli_side_symmetry: scripts/ai_status.py clears the review_decision_intent_recovery marker alongside review_decision_intent at every point the intent itself is cleared (command_reopen, abort_review_decision_intent, command_operator_accept, command_approve), so a completed or aborted replay never leaves a stale receipt behind.

safety_properties.no_impersonation: The recovery receipt's actor field is copied verbatim from the original intent at mint time under the exclusive canonical task-state lock; even if a wrong actor were ever dispatched, scripts/ai_status.py's enforce_pending_review_decision_fence independently re-validates current_actor() against the frozen intent, so the CLI itself refuses a mismatched replay regardless of what the supervisor dispatches.
safety_properties.generic_workers_fenced: review_decision_intent_replay_eligible() requires canonical_agent_name(agent_name) == canonical_agent_name(intent.actor); every other agent continues to see human_ops_hold=True / task_execution_dispatch_candidate() returning None.
safety_properties.stale_generation_rejection: review_decision_intent_recovery_is_current() requires exact equality on task_generation, task_digest, nonce, actor, command, and message; any drift (a bumped generation, a changed task, a different pending intent) makes the receipt non-current and the ordinary fence re-applies automatically.
safety_properties.no_premature_mutation: The recovery lane never calls command_approve/command_reopen/command_operator_accept, never bumps task generation, and never edits any field review_decision_task_digest depends on; it only ever authorizes one more dispatch of the original actor to run the CLI's own existing idempotent replay path.
